questions.q: State the six criteria that make a product suitable for mail order trading as per NCERT.
questions.a: The six criteria are: (i) graded and standardised, (ii) easily transported at low cost, (iii) ready demand in the market, (iv) available in large quantity throughout the year, (v) least possible competition, (vi) can be described through pictures/catalogues. A wrong answer (e.g., listing "perishable goods" or "high-value jewellery") reveals the student has memorised features without understanding the logistical and informational constraints that define mail order suitability.

questions.q: Explain why "high dependence on postal services" is listed as a limitation of mail order houses, and give one real-world situation where this limitation would critically fail.
questions.a: Mail order houses rely entirely on postal/courier networks for both order receipt and goods delivery; if postal services are disrupted, delayed, or absent in a region, the business cannot function. A critical failure situation: a mail order house trying to serve villages in Arunachal Pradesh where postal delivery takes 15-20 days and no courier operates. A wrong answer (e.g., "internet is slow") confuses mail order with e-commerce and misses the physical logistics dependency.

questions.q: Give the correct order of criteria tests that decide whether handmade pottery suits mail order trading.
questions.a: The tests run: (1) Grading fails because each piece is unique and non-standardised (2) Transport fails because the fragile goods carry high breakage cost (3) Year-round bulk supply fails since artisans work made to order (4) Catalogue description fails because glaze and weight need touch, so the product is unsuitable overall. A wrong answer that relies on doorstep delivery as the answer shows the student has missed that all six suitability criteria must hold together.

questions.q: Compare the "elimination of middlemen" merit of mail order houses with that of departmental stores. In what fundamental way does the supply chain differ?
questions.a: Both eliminate middlemen, but departmental stores buy directly from manufacturers and operate their own warehouses (they *are* the retailer-warehouser), while mail order houses may be manufacturers themselves or single intermediaries who bypass wholesalers/retailers but still depend on postal logistics as the "distribution channel." The fundamental difference: departmental stores create a physical distribution hub; mail order houses substitute the entire physical retail chain with a communication-and-postal chain. A wrong answer treating them as identical misses the structural difference in *how* middlemen are eliminated.

questions.q: "Mail order houses provide convenience to customers." Critique this statement by analysing two scenarios where this convenience is illusory for the buyer.
questions.a: Convenience is illusory when: (1) The buyer is illiterate or semi-literate — cannot read catalogues, fill order forms, or understand VPP terms, making the process inaccessible, not convenient. (2) The product requires trial/fitting (e.g., shoes, garments) — delayed delivery + no physical inspection + cumbersome return via post creates *inconvenience*. A wrong answer that only cites "doorstep delivery" as convenience shows surface-level understanding without evaluating the buyer's capability and product nature.

questions.q: Design a mail order business model for selling certified organic spices to urban households across India. Specify: (a) how you will overcome the "high promotion cost" limitation, (b) how you will address "no after-sales service" for quality complaints, (c) one product-line modification to meet "graded and standardised" criterion.
questions.a: (a) Overcome promotion cost: Use targeted digital ads (low cost) driving traffic to a free downloadable PDF catalogue + WhatsApp ordering, reducing print/postage spend. (b) Address after-sales: Include a toll-free number and QR code on packaging for instant quality complaints; offer replacement via courier (not post) at company cost for verified issues. (c) Product modification: Sell only pre-packed, FSSAI-certified, fixed-weight (50g/100g) spice blends with batch numbers and expiry dates — not loose spices. A poor answer suggests "advertise more on TV" (increases cost) or "ignore complaints" (violates consumer protection), showing inability to innovate within constraints.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Mail order houses are retail trading ______ that sell goods exclusively through postal or courier communication without any physical store or direct personal contact between buyer and seller, where orders are solicited via catalogues, advertisements, or samples and goods are dispatched by post or courier upon receipt of payment (advance, VPP, or bank-mediated).
Fill in the blank: Imagine you live in a remote village in Rajasthan where the nearest ______ mall is 200 km away.
What is Mail order houses? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: Mail order houses are retail trading establishments that sell goods exclusively through postal or courier communication without any physical store or direct personal contact between buyer and seller, where orders are solicited via catalogues, advertisements, or samples and goods are dispatched by post or courier upon receipt of payment.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Imagine you live in a remote village in Rajasthan where the nearest shopping mall is ______ km away.
What common mix-up does this lesson flag about Mail order houses?
questions.a: Students often confuse mail order houses with e-commerce (online shopping), assuming they are the same because both involve "ordering from home." They then incorrectly attribute features like "instant order confirmation," "digital payment," "real-time tracking," or "easy returns" to mail order houses.

questions.q: What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to: (1) Distinguish mail order houses from other non-store retail formats (e.g., e-commerce, teleshopping) based on the role of postal infrastructure and absence of digital interface; (2) Evaluate the suitability of a given product for mail order trade using the six NCERT criteria with justification; (3).
